claims.statement: The Rust gateway is an optional executor on the model traffic path that makes no privacy or memory decisions of its own; every allow, block, and withhold verdict comes from PowerContext Core and the gateway only executes them in order.

The gateway README declares the gateway a working prototype verified end to end against a PowerContext Server branch (PR #2264), and it depends on the /v1/context/check contract and include_reuse from #2264.
The executor runs the phases in strict order: check before_send, then send admitted bytes only after an allow, then check before_release on the complete upstream response, then capture and release.
The binding returned by Core at before_send is reused as request_binding at before_release, so the release verdict is bound to the exact send-phase admission.

An allow verdict is accepted only if it has the expected schema, the expected phase, a non-empty binding, and complete coverage when Core advertises enforcing; any other allow is a malformed verdict that pauses the gate, so HTTP success alone is never treated as approval.

Each send attempt and the release verdict are checked against their valid_until deadline, and a deadline that has passed or cannot be parsed returns admission_expired without sending or releasing content, failing closed; the deadline is also rechecked after capture.
The fully rendered request body is measured against the input limit before the before_send check, and a body over the limit is blocked with request_payload_too_large without any Core check.

A release-phase block invokes Transport::cancel and returns a block outcome, so no upstream content is released to the client; the reqwest transport's cancel is a no-op because the response is already fully buffered.

The ingress maps outcomes to client statuses: released passes through upstream status and content type; block returns 403; withhold returns 400 unless every reason is context-refresh-required, which returns 409; send_indeterminate and not_sent return 502; admission_expired returns 409; gate_paused returns 503; a deadline stop returns 504 and a shutdown or cancellation stop returns 503.

Core unreachable (GateUnavailable) pauses model traffic by default with 503 gate_paused; the gateway sends a pristine request without memory only when PC_GATEWAY_DEGRADE is passthrough and the startup capabilities query succeeded with enforcing false.

Degradation is permitted only when Core's capabilities report enforcing=false at startup; a failed or invalid capabilities query leaves degradation disabled, and Core computes enforcing as mode equal to enforcing.
Blocked verdicts never degrade: a block returns before the degradation branch, and only an unreachable Core can degrade, so malformed or rejected Core replies pause the gate with 503 gate_paused.
A degraded passthrough sends the pristine request without injected memory, makes no before_release check and records no capture, and marks the response with the x-pc-degraded header.

Retry is limited to attempts confirmed not sent; each NotSent attempt re-runs before_send to obtain a fresh admission before the next send, and the total number of attempts, including the first, is capped by PC_GATEWAY_MAX_ATTEMPTS with a default of 2.
The reqwest transport reports NotSent only for connect and request-builder failures; timeouts and any failure after the request may have reached the provider are Indeterminate.
An indeterminate send is never retried: a connection lost after handoff or a timeout returns send_indeterminate immediately, because the provider may already have billed the request.

Upstream responses are buffered up to 1 MiB by default, and exceeding the cap returns withheld with response_buffer_limit_exceeded, which the client receives as HTTP 400, without releasing content or resending the request.

The Core-facing UDS client retries a failed operation at most once, on the first attempt, only when the failure is a GateUnavailable error and either the operation is replay-safe (check, capabilities, capture) or no request bytes were handed off; read timeouts after a write count as handed off, and non-2xx rejections are never retried.

When injection applies to a request, the gateway prepares memory through Core's prepare contract with the last user message as the query, include_reuse enabled, a memory-only assembly and an 8192-byte cap; a failed prepare injects nothing, is not cached, and never blocks the request, while an empty result injects nothing.

Injected memory is placed verbatim in the last user message, and the exact UTF-8 byte range is declared in prepared_contexts; Core checks that range's length and SHA-256 digest against the verified reuse and rejects a mismatch, so the gateway cannot alter injected bytes undetected.

With a conversation ID, requests that share a message anchor reuse the exact prepared block and binding from an in-memory replay cache, bounded by five minutes and the reuse expiry, and a new user message prepares once; requests without a conversation ID prepare independently and inherit no injection.

The conversation ID comes from X-PowerContext-Conversation-ID first, then from Claude Code, OpenCode, or Codex session headers, and each source carries a distinct prefix so identifiers from different sources cannot collide.

When Core withholds with context-refresh-required on a request that had prepared contexts, the gateway forgets that conversation's replay entry, restores the pristine request, and repeats enrich and check once, so a stale reuse dependency is refreshed instead of reaching the client.

Injection scope defaults to conversations only in a combined deployment and to off in a standalone deployment; on and off are explicit, any unrecognized value disables injection, and PC_GATEWAY_INJECTION_RESPONSES=off disables injection on the Responses route only.

When sedimentation is enabled, each released turn with a transcript is captured after its release verdict passes, using a source ID derived from the scope, the conversation ID, and the pre-injection messages when a conversation exists; a 409 conflict is reported through the legacy record_not_sent hook as sediment_duplicate, and a failed capture never blocks the release.

The Responses route always sends a non-streaming upstream request, while the Chat route forwards the client's stream flag; a Responses client that asked for streaming receives the released 200 response replayed as Responses SSE events only after the release gate passes, and error statuses are returned as plain JSON.

In the combined deployment, selected by PC_GATEWAY_CORE_UDS, the gateway owns the public port, reverse-proxies non-gateway routes to Core over a Unix socket, and talks to Core over that socket; in the standalone deployment it talks to Core over HTTP and serves only /gateway/v1 and /healthz, returning 404 for other routes.

Core calls use the same GateClient operations in both deployment forms: check to /v1/context/check, prepare to /v1/context/prepare, capture to /v1/sources/content, and capabilities to /v1/capabilities; the HTTP client uses a 10-second request timeout, a 3-second connect timeout, and no redirects.

The model input limit is the minimum of the Core payload capacity, the 1 MiB Core parser ceiling, and PC_GATEWAY_MAX_BODY_BYTES, and if startup capabilities cannot be obtained or are incompatible the model routes stay paused until restart.

Middleware rejects model request bodies whose Content-Length exceeds the limit with 413, rejects model routes with zero capacity with 503, applies a non-queuing concurrency limit that returns 503 when full, and exempts the health probe.

Upstream and Core credentials come only from server-side environment variables, never from request fields, and the header set forwarded in check payloads strips authorization, x-api-key, and cookie so provider credentials never enter Core payloads.

The evidence sink records body-free facts only, such as attempt counts, not-sent and indeterminate reasons, usage completeness, cache reads, and first-byte and release timings, and never request or response bodies.

The Core client, upstream transport, and middleware chain are extension points: the executor depends only on the GateClient trait, the upstream path accepts only AdmittedSend values through the Transport trait, and new middleware is added to a chain composed in main.

A non-enforcing Core still inspects before_send but does not inspect before_release, and it returns allow with incomplete privacy coverage rather than withhold; the gateway accepts those allows only because startup detected non-enforcing operation.

When PC_GATEWAY_API_KEY is set, model routes require exactly one Bearer credential that matches it in constant time, and a missing or mismatched credential returns 401 invalid_gateway_key before any Core call; a non-loopback listener refuses to start without a key.
When PC_GATEWAY_UPSTREAM_URL_RESPONSES is empty, the Responses route returns 501 responses_route_disabled before any Core call, so no default third-party upstream is used.

Each model request runs under one absolute 180-second deadline, and a lifecycle stop at any checkpoint returns its stop reason: deadline expiry returns 504, while shutdown or cancellation returns 503.

A SIGINT or SIGTERM closes model admission at once, so calls not yet handed off stop with GatewayShutdown; the drain deadline is 25 seconds after the first signal, and an independent watchdog thread exits the process at 30 seconds.

The JSON evidence sink queues at most 1024 records on a bounded channel submitted with try_send, drops the newest record when the queue is full or a record is invalid, counts the loss, and never blocks a request.

The EvidenceSink trait's record_attempt and record_not_sent hooks are no-ops in the production JSON sink, so executor notes such as sediment_duplicate and degraded_passthrough reach only test or demo collectors, while per-call and per-attempt records are exported.
The transport crate no longer exports BoundedRetry or RetryOutcome, so model retries are owned only by the Executor.

The HTTP Core client makes at most two attempts per operation, retrying a first-attempt send error only for connect failures or replay-safe operations (check, capabilities, capture), and it returns non-2xx responses as GateRejected without retry.
